The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer making the reclassification retroactive to 1985, six years prior to the audit in 1991.

DecKeywords: Pensions (assessment) (chronic pain); Supplements, temporary; Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker fell at work in April 1984 injuring her shoulder and low back.  She returned to lighter work with the accident employer in December 1984.  The worker had surgery for a non-compensable condition in February 1986 and did not return to work with the accident employer.  In June 1986, the worker began working part-time with her husband's business.  She continued in this position until January 1990 when she stopped working because there was not enough work and because she was not feeling well enough.  The worker did not return to any further work.  She was awarded a 10% pension for chronic pain disability retroactive to July 1987.  That level was confirmed in June 1991 but was raised to 15%, effective May 1992.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Withdrawal (of appeal)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting ongoing entitlement after January 1992.  The Hearings Officer limited her decision to the issue of whether the worker had returned to his pre-accident state in January 1992.  Therefore, the Panel did not have jurisdiction over the issue of suitability of modified work in June 1992.

DecKeywords: Penalties; Board Directives and Guidelines (penalty assessments) (homogeneous rate group); Parties (participation) (Board); Parties (Board)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming a penalty assessment on the employer for the years 1984-1986.
The worker was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying additional VR services.  The worker claimed that he required training in English as a second language.
The worker suffered a low back injury in 1982.  He was awarded a 20% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming the level of the pension.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [6 pages]

The worker suffered compensable knee injuries when he tripped at work in April 1989 and June 1990.  The worker underwent a high tibial osteotomy in February 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits for the osteotomy.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (program not offered by Board); Supplements, temporary; Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1986.  In Decision No. 90/90, the Tribunal found that the worker was entitled to full temporary benefits until March 1988.  After that, the Board continued to pay 50% benefits.  The worker was later granted a 15% pension and supplement retroactive to March 1988.  On appeal by the employer, the supplement was revoked.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying supplementary benefits from March 1988 to April 1992.
The worker suffered a back strain in 1991 while lifting a desk.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for recurrences in 1992 and 1993.
The worker suffered a back injury while working as a bellman at a hotel in 1980.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a s. 147 supplement.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (vacation pay); Reconsideration (consideration of evidence)
DecSummary: The worker applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 13/96 in which the Panel found that the worker's earnings basis, calculated on the basis of his hourly rate pursuant to s. 40(1)(a), should not include an additional amount that the worker received as vacation pay.

The worker suffered a back injury in June 1988.  The employer was granted 50% SIEF relief in July 1993.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying retroactive adjustment of its voluntary experience rating (VER) assessment.
The worker was awarded a 4.5% pension for noise-induced hearing loss in 1985.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the pension.

The worker appealed a decision which denied her entitlement to temporary total disability benefits, subsequent to June 1992, for back injuries sustained when she tripped on stairs in August 1991.  A few days after the accident, she returned to modified work which mostly involved entering data on the stock room computer, but she stopped working in June 1992.  The worker was granted an 8% NEL award for chronic pain in December 1993 and was denied a FEL award on the grounds that suitable work at no wage loss was available to her.  However, the only issue to be determined was whether there was a worsening of the worker's condition in June 1992 such that she was temporarily totally disabled.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1989.  He was awarded a 15% pension, which was later replaced by a 20% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming the 20% pension.

The employer appealed a decision entitling the worker to benefits beyond October 1989.  The worker, then aged 32, injured his back at work in August 1988.  He was diagnosed as suffering from a herniated disc and underwent an L4-5 discectomy in July 1989.  The worker was paid temporary total disability benefits for various periods until October 1989.  In January 1991, the worker requested benefits for a recurrence of his compensable injury.  The worker's temporary benefits were reinstated and he was awarded a 15% pension in March 1992.  In 1985 the worker had injured his back at work.  The employer was granted 75% SIEF relief with respect to the August 1988 accident, in recognition of the worker's pre-existing condition.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: A 65-year-old worker suffered right epicondylitis in 1990 from the repetitive nature of his work.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying SIEF relief.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered left elbow disability, diagnosed as epicondylitis, and received benefits from June 1993 to November 1993.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying SIEF relief.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the worker's 5% pension for residual symptoms from a ventral hernia.

A truck driver suffered an injury for which he was awarded a 20% pension, valued at about $77,000.  He is currently employed as an instructor at a truck driving training school.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a commutation of his pension in order to buy a truck.
The worker, a miner, appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss.

The worker suffered contusions to his abdomen in 1962.  He was awarded a 5% pension for chronic pain, effective March 27, 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147(4) benefits after July 26, 1989.

DecKeywords: Arising out of employment (intoxication); In the course of employment (employer's premises); Sailor
DecSummary: The worker was a seaman.  He was returning to his ship after shore leave of about three and one-half hours.  He fell from a ladder as he was climbing to board the ship.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the accident.

A farm manager suffered a low back injury in September 1992, when he was kicked in the stomach by a steer and thrown back against a wall.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits after February 1993.

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition) (asthma); Availability for employment (retirement); Permanent disability
DecSummary: The worker worked in a mining, smelting and refinery operation from 1973 to 1991.  He was granted benefits for aggravation of a preexisting a respiratory condition.  In 1991, the worker accepted an early retirement package from the employer.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying VR services and denying a pension.
The worker strained his neck at work in January 1985.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after February 1986 and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting the worker entitlement for an accident that occurred while the worker was on coffee break.  The worker was a helper truck driver.  He usually was on the road and took his coffee break wherever he was at the time.  However, there were some days when he worked in the shop.  On a day when the worker was in the shop, he went across the road for coffee at a restaurant and suffered a severe ankle strain while crossing.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1985 for which he was awarded a 15% pension.  The worker received s. 147(4) supplementary benefits after November 1989 but received no supplement from May 1988 to November 1989.  The worker appealed denial of the supplement during that period.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a psychological condition.

The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying further VR services.  The worker claimed that a work trial failed because treatment for his tendonitis condition was not appropriate and actually made his condition worse due to undiagnosed osteoarthritis.
The worker and employer both appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer which found that the worker suffered an accident on September 8, 1993, but was entitled to benefits for three days only.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back strain.

The worker suffered arm, back, hip and neck injuries when he slipped and fell on ice in February 1990, but did not lose any time from work.  The worker stopped working in January 1991 due to headaches, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, tinnitus and depression.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain in 1991.

The worker suffered a shoulder strain in December 1992.  The Board found that he could return to work in December 1993.  He did not return to work until the beginning of January 1994.  He stopped work again at the end of January 1994.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary total disability benefits from December 1993 to the beginning of January 1994 and after January 1994, and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

DecKeywords: Independent operator (truck driver); Right to sue
DecSummary: The issue in this s. 17 application was whether the respondent was a worker under the Act.

The worker's son appealed a decision of the Board denying entitlement for the worker's death from cancer.  The worker was a gold miner.  On the evidence, he died from cancer of the esophagus, not lung cancer.  Evidence did not establish a relationship between cancer of the esophagus and gold mining.

DecKeywords: Construction; Earnings basis (short or casual employment); Non-economic loss {NEL} (second assessment) (time limits)
DecSummary: The worker was injured in June 1990.  He was originally granted a zero NEL award but on appeal, was granted an assessment.  The NEL assessment was conducted but the employer requested a second assessment.  The worker refused to attend and the Board suspended benefits.  Benefits were originally established at the maximum of $42,000, but on appeal by the employer, were reduced to $19,000.  The worker appealed.

The worker started work as a forester in 1972 at age 21.  He had compensable accidents in 1977, for which he was off work for three weeks, and in 1988 and 1989, for which he did not lose time.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying ongoing entitlement for neck and back problems after February 1990.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (proceeding to and from work) (employer's vehicle); Right to sue
DecSummary: The issue in this s. 17 application was whether the driver and two passengers of a van were in the course of their employment at the time of a motor vehicle accident.  All three were workers of the same Schedule 1 employer.  The two passengers brought court actions arising from the accident.
The hearing was adjourned as it was apparent that the worker and his representative were not prepared.  [4 pages]

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying SIEF relief.  The Panel required additional evidence about a non-compensable motor vehicle accident and chiropractic treatment received by the worker, prior to making its decision.  [6 pages]

The worker appeared at the hearing of her appeal without her representative.  The representative sent a fax to the Tribunal the day before the hearing stating that he would not be appearing due to 'conflicted interest.'  The worker learned that the representative would not be appearing when informed of the fax by Tribunal counsel.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board)
DecSummary: A teacher suffered a left knee injury in a fall in 1990 and a right knee injury in a fall in 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying ongoing benefits from August 1993 to September 1994.
The worker suffered a fracture of the left ankle in 1956.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for gout in the right leg diagnosed in 1993.

A housekeeping aide suffered a low back injury while lifting a patient in February 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain and denying full temporary benefits after October 1993.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of issue)
DecSummary: The worker sought leave to appeal a decision of the WCB Appeal Board which held that he was not entitled benefits after 1976.  The worker hurt his back in August 1970 while lifting.  As x-rays revealed the presence of a compression fracture at the L2 level, the claim was allowed on the basis of an aggravation of a preexisting condition.  The worker received benefits until his return to work in October 1970.  He experienced further difficulty in January 1971 and benefits were again paid.  The worker was employed from 1971 until 1976 when he laid off due to his back condition.  The Appeal Board found that the worker's continuing back problems were related to the preexisting compression fracture and that he had recovered from the effects of the compensable lumbar muscle strain which arose out of the 1970 accident.

The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that it breached its re-employment obligations.  In this decision, the Panel dealt with the preliminary issue of whether the Tribunal was estopped from hearing the appeal.

The worker suffered a left knee injury in 1984 for which he was awarded a 30% pension.  The worker fell at home in 1987, injuring his right knee.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the right knee injury.
A dock worker suffered a low back strain while lifting a box in September 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits after May 1992.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (temporary partial disability) (Canada Pension Plan)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer reducing his temporary partial disability benefits by the amount of CPP benefits he was receiving.  The Panel agreed with Board policy to reduce benefits in accordance with s. 37(3) by the amount of CPP benefits.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to benefits for hearing loss.  It was accepted that the worker was exposed to hazardous noise.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying partial commutation of his pension, valued at about $154,000, which the worker wanted for the purpose of debt liquidation and business investment.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (supplements, temporary) (extension); Supplements, temporary
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1983 for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  He also received temporary supplementary benefits from January 1985 to December 1987.  On appeal, the Hearings Officer extended supplementary benefits until March 1988.  The worker appealed denial of temporary supplementary benefits until July 1989.

The accident employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer refusing to transfer the costs of a claim to another employer.  The accident employer had a trailer at a construction site that was used as a field office.  Ordinarily, there was a set of steel stairs to enable access to the trailer.  Someone removed the stairs and replaced them with a wooden skid.  The worker was injured when he fell as he was climbing down the skid.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1989 for which he was awarded a pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147 supplementary benefits from 1991 to 1994.
The worker's representative could not attend the hearing due to illness.  Relying on advice from the representative, the worker did not attend the hearing either.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Consequences of injury; Intervening causes; Rehabilitation, vocational (program not offered by Board); Supplements, transitional provisions
DecSummary: In December 1987, the worker's hand and arm were caught in a roller causing fractures of the forearm and requiring the attachment of metal plates.  The worker had been hired as a supervisor shortly before the accident, but was performing the work of a machine operator.  In August 1988 his doctor recommended that he return to work as a supervisor.  In September 1988 the worker returned to work as an assistant supervisor but he stopped after less than two hours due to pain in his arm.  A few days later, the worker was involved in an automobile accident.  He used his injured arm to restrain himself during the impact and this caused him increased pain.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (average weekly earnings); Hearing (oral); Natural justice (oral hearing)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of temporary benefits for a one-week period.

The employer applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 882/96.  The employer submitted that the hearing panel failed to refer in the decision to a report of an ergonomist that was referred to extensively in the hearing and to a videotape that was viewed by the hearing panel.

The Board granted benefits to the worker for epicondylitis.  The Hearings Officer found that epicondylitis is an occupational disease but refused to transfer the costs of the claim to the employer's rate group.  The employer appealed.

The worker suffered cervical injuries from a gunshot in a non-compensable accident in 1972.  In February 1990, he slipped and fell in a compensable accident.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits after October 1991.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a left wrist and thumb injury.  The Panel found the worker to be a credible witness.  The Panel found that the worker suffered a back spasm related to her compensable back injury at home while she was bathing her baby.  While putting the baby down, she took the weight of the baby on her left wrist and thumb and suffered a sudden onset of pain.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of his pension, valued at about $60,000, which he wanted in order to purchase a house where he will live with his family and operate a hairdressing business.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (aid in getting worker back to work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a shoulder injury in 1987 for which he was awarded a 5% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying VR services after June 1992.
The worker's widow was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic obstructive lung disease which the appellant related to the worker's exposure to dust.
The worker did not appear for the hearing of his appeal.  When contacted later, the worker stated that he had a panic attack and went to see his doctor.
The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer imposing the maximum penalty on the employer for breach of its re-employment obligations.

DecKeywords: Notice of accident (prejudice); Significant contribution (of employment to disability)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying initial entitlement for a back condition which the worker claimed arose out of and in the course of employment in April 1981.  The worker claimed that he was working with dusty boxes that came from the company archives.  He sneezed twice and felt an immediate onset of back pain.  He returned to work in September 1981 after having surgery.  He worked until June 1982 when he had further surgery.  He has not returned to work.
The worker was appealing termination of temporary benefits for three separate accidents and refusal to make an award for chronic pain retroactive to 1986.

DecKeywords: Causation (thin skull doctrine); Transfer of costs
DecSummary: The worker suffered a shoulder injury at work in August 1986.  In September 1986, he underwent surgery.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the surgery.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a compensable injury in June 1993.  In August 1993, he returned to modified work but stopped work again after two hours.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker refused suitable employment.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (program not offered by Board)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain from lifting in July 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits after January 1994.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying partial commutation of his pension, valued at about $210,000, for the purpose of debt liquidation and vehicle purchase.
The worker's appeal was withdrawn at the request of the worker.  [4 pages]
Two employers appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer apportioning the costs of a claim equally between them rather than to the class in which the employers operate.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after December 1992.  On the evidence, work offered by the accident employer was not suitable for the worker considering her physical restrictions.
The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer attributing the costs of a claim for epicondylitis to the employer rather than to the class in which the employer operates.

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker was in the course of employment at the time of a motor vehicle accident while travelling from her home in Hamilton to a motel in London where she was to meet the rest of her work crew.
The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer attributing the costs of a claim for carpal tunnel syndrome to the employer rather than to the class in which the employer operates.

The worker slipped and fell in January 1993.  He continued to work until May 1993.  He underwent surgery in December 1993.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting benefits from May 1993 to December 1993.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a NEL award for permanent impairment of the back.

DecKeywords: Accident (occurrence); Benefit of the doubt; Continuing entitlement
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying initial entitlement for an accident in January 1992 and for a recurrence in September 1992.

The worker was struck on the side of the face with an axe in January 1970.  He did not lose consciousness and did not lose time from work but he did require stitches.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for headaches which the worker claimed were related to the 1970 accident.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back injury.  The worker claimed that he suffered the injury on the morning of May 26, 1993, when he lifted castings at work.  The Panel found that an accident did not occur.  There was evidence from four witnesses that the worker arrived to work late on May 26 and that he did not actually perform any work that morning.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition); Medical report (clinical notes); Second accident
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement from December 1992 to August 1993 for aggravation at work of a preexisting back condition.

The worker was a truck driver who suffered a compensable whiplash in 1990.  The Board sponsored the worker in a 32-week course in marine and small engine repair.  Midway through the course, the worker had to choose between marine engine and small engine repair.  The worker chose small engine repair and successfully completed the course.  The worker wanted further sponsorship to complete the course in marine engine repair.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying the further sponsorship and denying further VR services.

The worker developed compensable heel spurs from his work as a tire builder, for which he was awarded a 7.5% pension.  Because of the heel condition, he was transferred to the job of serviceman.  In this job, he would check and deliver tires, using a tugger machine to make the deliveries.  The worker developed chondromalacia patella.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the knee condition.

A construction worker suffered a right leg, right shoulder and low back injury in June 1988, and a low back injury in May 1972.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a neck condition which the worker claimed he also suffered in the compensable accidents.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Future economic loss {FEL} (pre-injury earnings); Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain in December 1990, as he was twisting and lifting a 20 pound bundle of paper.  In April 1991, the worker fractured his ankle when he fell, in an incident that did not occur at work.  In December 1992, the Board determined that the worker was entitled to a zero FEL award since he refused suitable modified work at no wage loss.  In 1993, he was awarded a 32% NEL award.  The worker appealed denial of entitlement for the ankle disability and denial of a FEL award.
The worker was no longer interested in pursuing the issue on appeal.  Rather, he was going to pursue other matters at the Board.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation) (earning capacity)
DecSummary: The worker was injured in 1988 while working as a welder.  He had previously worked at various sales and purchasing jobs, as well as other welding jobs.  In 1991 he was awarded a 30% pension for chronic pain disability.  The Board sponsored the worker in a year long law clerk program.  Upon graduation, he accepted a part-time  job training and working as a court registrar.  The Board paid the worker a s. 147(2) supplement.  The worker did not continue to work for the employer after December 1992 when it stopped offering steady work.  In March 1993, he opened his own video and billiards business.  His income from operating this business did not equal his pre-accident earnings, and he therefore requested a section 147(4) supplement.  His business was later destroyed in a fire.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement at the Board based on a new theory of the cause of the worker's disability arising from new medical evidence.  [4 pages]

The worker injured his back in March 1980, when a wrench slipped while he was loosening a bolt and caused him to twist his back.  He remained off work for a month and received compensation benefits.  The worker had a motorcycle accident in October 1980.  In October 1982 the worker changed jobs to work as a maintenance mechanic repairing printing presses.  This work involved heavy lifting in very awkward positions.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits after July 1988 for disability that the worker claimed was related to a compensable accident in November 1987.  The worker claimed that the accident permanently aggravated his preexisting psoriatic arthritis.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (prolonged disability)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision granting it only 75% SIEF relief.  The worker injured his low back in 1991 while carrying sheets of plywood up stairs.  He returned to work after five months.  The Hearings Officer characterized this accident as minor and the medical significance of the preexisting condition as moderate.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1973.  He was awarded a 15% pension for organic disability.  In 1992, a 5% pension for chronic pain was added to the organic award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming the level of the pension.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (right to sue) (initial entitlement); Right to sue; Supplier of motor vehicle, machinery or equipment
DecSummary: The issue in this s. 17 application was whether the accident which was the subject of a court action arose out of the plaintiff's employment.  The defendant Z, a co-worker of the plaintiff, sustained an eye injury at work.  One of the plaintiff's duties was to provide first aid.  In that capacity, the employer instructed her to take Z to the hospital.  A van leased by the employer was made available to the plaintiff for this task.  The plaintiff lost control of the van on the way to the hospital.  Both Z and the plaintiff were injured as a result.  The plaintiff claimed compensation benefits for the resulting disability.  There was no indication that any non-work-related factor contributed to the occurrence of the accident.

The worker suffered a knee injury in 1985 for which he was awarded an 18% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting 50% benefits for temporary disability from May 1993 to September 1993.

The employer withdrew its appeal of a decision granting dependency to the worker's widow.  The Panel refused the widow's request to remain seized of the matter in case the employer decides to appeal again.  However, the Panel noted that effort and resources had been expended on the appeal.  If the employer appeals again, the widow could refer to this proceeding.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Stress, mental
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision denying him entitlement to benefits for psychological disability due to occupational stress, either as a result of a specific new job undertaken by the worker in April 1988, or due to his general treatment at the workplace from 1980 to 1988.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying initial entitlement for accidents in August and September 1989.
The worker was absent for the hearing of her appeal due to a violent snow storm.  The hearing was adjourned.  [3 pages]
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a respiratory condition which the worker related to his work as an underground miner and in the pulp and paper industry.

The worker appealed a decision denying him further benefits for a back disability.  He had hurt his back in three work accidents in 1959, 1961 and 1975.  The worker did not miss much time from work as a result of these accidents but he was switched to lighter duties after the 1959 accident.  He worked until his retirement in 1981.  There was a gap in medical treatment from the late 1970s to 1987, but he made lifestyle adjustments at home as a result of the work injuries.  The Panel found that the worker was a credible witness and that his back problems had never resolved.  He should not be punished for being a stoic individual who had a desire to keep working.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1977 for which he was awarded a 10% pension and another back injury in 1984 for which he was awarded another 10% pension.  The worker elected to accept an early retirement package from the employer in 1984.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to a s. 147(4) supplement.

In January 1972, the worker was struck on the back by a falling branch.  He sustained a compression fracture at T-12.  In 1978 the worker was hit on the shoulder by a falling branch, while working in Quebec.  The worker's widow appealed a decision which denied the worker's 1979 request for entitlement to a pension for low back problems.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (peremptory hearing date); Procedure (absent parties); Procedure (production of documents)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement.  On the first day of hearing, the Panel directed the employer to produce further documents.  On the second day of the hearing, the worker was not present.  The worker's representative requested an adjournment due to inability to prepare because of late receipt of the documents.

The worker was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of benefits.  The worker raised an issue that the Board had not had an opportunity to consider.  The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to return to the Board.

A sewing machine operator suffered neck and back strain in April 1991 from lifting and pulling boxes of parts to make leather boots.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that a work trial in May 1992 was suitable for the worker.

The employer was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for chronic pain.  The worker was not present at the hearing.  Prior to the hearing, the worker's representative had submitted a written request for an adjournment since the worker was in California attending school.  The adjournment was refused by the Tribunal's Appeals Administrator.  The worker's representative renewed the request for adjournment at the hearing.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer which granted entitlement for right carpal tunnel syndrome but denied entitlement for left carpal tunnel syndrome.

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition) (diverticular disease); Benefit of the doubt; Consequences of injury (iatrogenic illness) (medication) (anti-inflammatory)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for rectal bleeding in November 1992 and August 1993.  The worker suffered a shoulder injury in 1988 for which he was taking pain and anti-inflammatory medication.  The worker claimed that the medication was a significant cause of the bleeding.

The employer was appealing a decision of the Reinstatement Officer regarding VR services.  Subsequently, the employer advised that it wanted to appeal a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding temporary benefits.

The worker suffered a major crush injury to his left ankle, for which he was awarded a 13% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for left and right knee and low back disabilities.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1989 for which she was awarded a 20% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits from April 1992 to July 1992 and from November 1992 to January 1993.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (participation in rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a knee injury in 1987 for which he was awarded a 3% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147(2) supplementary benefits from January 1992 to April 1994, denying entitlement for shoulder disability and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

The worker suffered shoulder and neck injuries in compensable accidents in January 1986 and November 1986.  The Board granted a 15% pension for neck disability resulting from the first accident and a 7% pension for shoulder disability resulting from the second accident, retroactive to the dates of the accidents.  Later, the Board decided that the permanent neck disability resulted from the second accident and that, accordingly, the pension for neck disability should have been retroactive to November 1986 rather than January 1986.  The worker appealed.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a neck injury which the worker claimed he also suffered in the compensable accident.
The worker suffered an eye injury in 1967 for which he was awarded a pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Mediation Officer denying a wage loss supplement from 1975 to 1983.

The worker was exposed to mercury while working in the 'jig room' at various times from 1970 to 1980.  He was removed from the jig room after urine samples showed high levels of mercury.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for various gastrointestinal problems which the worker related to the mercury exposure.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying initial entitlement for a back injury in 1987.

DecKeywords: Cashier; Disablement (nature of work); Disc, herniated
DecSummary: The worker began work as a part-time cashier in 1987.  She began complaining of back pain in 1990.  A herniated disc was diagnosed in 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement.
The worker was struck on the head by a pole in October 1974 and received benefits until January 1975.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Adjudicator denying benefits after January 1975.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1984 for which she was awarded a 15% pension.  She returned to modified work at the end of May 1990 but stopped working after a few days.  The Board granted temporary benefits in June and July 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after July 1990.

The worker applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 1202/96.  The worker submitted a new letter from her doctor supporting entitlement.  The hearing panel had 24 reports from this doctor concerning the worker's condition, none of which related the condition to her work.  The new letter supported entitlement but did not set out the evidence on which he based the opinion.

The worker suffered a low back injury in November 1989.  He returned to modified work in July 1990 but stopped working after four hours due to increased back pain.  Full temporary benefits were reinstated until October 1990 and 50% benefits until November 1990, when a 15% pension was assessed.  In 1992, the pension was increased to 25% due to chronic pain with full retroactivity.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits after October 1990 and denying s. 147(4) supplementary benefits.

The worker suffered knee and hip injuries when she slipped and fell off a short ladder in December 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a low back injury which the worker claimed she also suffered in the compensable accident.
The employer requested clarification of Decision No. 591/96 in which the Panel allowed the employer's appeal and granted interest to the employer.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (period of unemployment); Earnings basis (short or casual employment)
DecSummary: The worker had been working for the accident employer since 1987.  He was injured in 1992.  The Board originally based benefits on his hourly rate.  However, it later recalculated benefits based on his earnings over the year preceding the accident, after it was determined that the worker was subject to a federal employment regulation, known as an exclusion order, pursuant to which the worker could not work more than 129 days per year.  The worker appealed.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to purse related matters currently before the Board.

DecKeywords: Accident (occurrence); Available employment (offer from accident employer); Benefit of the doubt
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting initial entitlement for an accident in November 1993 and ongoing entitlement for three weeks.

The worker appealed a decision which denied him benefits for a heart attack sustained in November 1990.  The worker, who was then 65 years old, worked in a factory's receiving department.  He was responsible for the unloading of supplies for the plant.  The worker spent most of his day driving a forklift, but he was sometimes required to handle some of the smaller rolls of paper, occasionally weighing over 100 pounds, and do some lifting.  In July 1990, a co-worker laid off from work, so that the worker's workload increased.  September and October were busy months and in October the worker had to do inventory by himself for the first time.  He worked an unusually heavy 12 days without a break before taking a weekend off.  The worker suffered the heart attack on the Monday that he returned.

The worker suffered a crush injury to his left hand in 1987, resulting in amputation of four fingers.  He was awarded a 26.5% pension.  He returned to work and had been working as a contract labourer since October 1992, when, in March 1993, he was assaulted by a co-worker as he was attempting to break up a fight.  He suffered further left hand injuries in the assault when the co-worker kicked his hand and slammed his hand against a wall.  The worker's employment was terminated at the end of his contract in April 1993.  In 1995, the worker was assessed for a NEL award.  He was rated for a 28% NEL award, from which the 26.5% pension was deducted, leaving a NEL award of 1.5%.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits after April 1993.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (concurrent employment); Earnings basis (net average earnings) (income tax)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of benefits.  The worker had concurrent employment with two of his uncles.  He was injured while working for one of the uncles at $12 per hour.  The Board originally based earnings on a 40-hour week at $12 per hour.  It also compared the $500 a week the worker could expect to earn with the $750 a week the worker could expect from his part-time job and his regular job, and adopted $500, the lesser amount as the appropriate earnings basis.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 92/96 was denied.  The worker alleged that his representative was inexperienced and that her presentation of the case was unsatisfactory.  The Panel was of the view that the representative conducted herself in a most professional manner and that there was no inadequacy in the presentation of the case.  There were no other defects in the proceedings.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition); Benefit of the doubt
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1986 for which he was granted a 15% pension.  He suffered a further injury in March 1992 as he and a co-worker lifted a heavy tool box down from a locker.  The Board granted benefits for aggravation of the low back condition until November 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying further benefits for low back disability and denying entitlement for thoracic spine disability.

The worker suffered a back injury in August 1992.  He returned to work in November 1992 and worked irregularly, at a reduced rate of pay, until he suffered another accident in December 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the employer did not breach its re-employment obligations.

The worker suffered a shoulder and neck injury in 1988.  In 1995, she was awarded a 15% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability from 1994 to 1995.
A nursing assistant suffered a muscle strain in 1975 while lifting a patient.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension.

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for a gradual onset of right elbow pain at work on May 21, 1992.  The employer submitted that the worker fabricated the claim in response to the employer's decision to lay him off.  The Panel accepted the worker's evidence of the onset of pain at work and that the employer had a practice of laying off workers who complained of injury.

The worker suffered a crush injury to his foot when a truck ran over his foot in 1987.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker did not suffer a permanent disability.
The hearing of the worker's appeal was adjourned to allow the worker to obtain a final decision from the Board on a number of issues.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of evidence); Leave to appeal (substantial new evidence) (medical report)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying a pension for permanent disability resulting from a repetitive strain injury in 1974.  There was substantial new evidence of continuing complaint on a regular basis long after the Appeal Board decision.  There was also good reason to doubt correctness of the Appeal Board decision due to internal contradictions in the findings as to whether there evidence of organic disability.

DecKeywords: Intervening causes (undermotivation); Rehabilitation, vocational (benefit from rehabilitation); Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation) (earning capacity) (personal characteristics of worker)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in June 1983 and was granted a 10% pension.  He was provided with training to become a cabinetmaker.  He worked in this capacity for some years, but subsequently was unable to find employment.  The worker was granted a s. 147(4) supplement from July 1989 to 1993, when the Board concluded that the worker's vocational rehabilitation services had given him the ability to approximate his pre-injury earnings, and that his wage loss at that time was due to economic factors, rather than his compensable injury.  The Board thus found that the worker was not entitled to further vocational rehabilitation services or to a further supplement.

The worker appealed a decision denying him entitlement for an emotional condition which he characterized as disablement from chronic workplace stress, or alternatively, as a psychotraumatic disability caused by a specific traumatic workplace event in April 1990.
The worker suffered a back strain in February 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for septic discitis and osteomyelitis.
The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying dependency benefits for the worker's death.  She also appealed a decision of the Board to collect a small overpayment.

The worker suffered a neck and shoulder injury in 1977 when he was struck by a rock.  He suffered a compensable aggravation of his condition in 1988, which was treated as a disablement.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying benefits for neck and shoulder disability in 1994.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in his 2% NEL award.  After the Hearings Officer decision was released, the Board granted further entitlement based on accepting a new diagnosis as related to the compensable injury.  As a result, the worker was entitled to a redetermination of his NEL award.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (cooperation); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker injured his back at work in October 1991, when he slipped on ice.  The worker made unsuccessful attempts to return to work in December 1992 and April 1993.  He refused to participate in further work trials.  His VR file was closed in May 1993.  The worker returned to modified work in June 1993, but stopped shortly afterwards, claiming a recurrence.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying VR services after May 1993 and denying temporary benefits after June 1993.

DecKeywords: Agreement (parties); Suitable employment; Procedure (agreed statement of facts); Supplements, FEL
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer that granted entitlement for chronic pain and increased her NEL award from 11% to 15% but denied a FEL supplement after October 1993.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [4 pages]
The worker was struck on the arm in June 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for arm disability in May 1991.

DecKeywords: Continuing entitlement; Psychotraumatic disability; Rehabilitation, vocational (benefit from rehabilitation); Temporary partial disability (duration of benefits)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a burn injury at work in April 1992.  Benefits were terminated in May 1993.  On appeal to the Hearings Officer, 50% benefits for temporary partial disability were granted from May 1993 to February 1994.  The worker appealed denial of full temporary benefits after May 1993 and denial of further VR services.

The worker slipped and fell in 1980, suffering leg, neck and low back injuries.  He was awarded a 25% pension for low back disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for shoulder disability and psychotraumatic disability and denying an increase in the pension for low back disability.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% benefits for a period in June 1993 for epicondylitis.  The hearing was adjourned at the worker's request to allow the worker to obtain further evidence.
The worker was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain.
The worker suffered a number of charley horses at work in 1958 and 1959. The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for leg surgery in the 1960s.
The worker was granted benefits in October 1989 for shoulder pain on a disablement basis.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for back disability.

In Decision No. 311/96I, the Panel increased the worker's pension for chronic pain to 30% retroactive to 1991.  In this decision, the Panel dealt with the worker's entitlement to temporary benefits for a number of periods from 1992 to 1995.
The Panel reconsidered Decision No. 24/96 to determine entitlement to temporary supplementary benefits under s. 43(5) of the pre-1985 Act.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue a final decision at the Board regarding some of the issues on appeal.  [5 pages]
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for chronic pain at the Board.

A 56-year-old carpenter suffered chest pain at work on October 14, 1989, after pulling a cord a number of times to start a chainsaw.  On October 18, he awoke with more severe chest pain.  He then went to the hospital where it was concluded that he suffered a minor heart attack.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the heart attack.
The worker suffered a back injury in 1980 for which she was off work for one week.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement in 1989.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation) (earning capacity)
DecSummary: The worker suffered compensable injuries for which he was awarded a 20% pension for psychological disability and a 15% pension for back disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147(4) supplementary benefits after March 1992.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (appealable issue); Jurisdiction, Tribunal (right to sue) (subrogation); Right to sue; Subrogation
DecSummary: The plaintiff in a court action, B, was injured  when an overhead door fell on him.  In Decision No. 299/92, the panel found that B was in the course of his employment at the time of his accident and that, pursuant to s. 10(9) his right of action was taken away with respect to his employer and other Schedule 1 employers.  However, under s. 10(10) B's action against K Ltd, the manufacturer of the door, was not taken away.  The Decision No. 299/92 panel also found that, as B had applied for and received compensation benefits, his right of action against K Ltd which survived under s. 10(1), was subrogated to the Board pursuant to s. 10(4).

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1979.  In 1995, he was granted a 15% pension retroactive to 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying pension arrears to the date of the accident.

In Decision No. 1001/96, the Panel found that the conduct of the worker's representative fell short of the appropriate standard of courtesy and respect which should be given to a Tribunal panel.  The Panel stated that if it did not receive a written apology, it would refer the matter to the Tribunal Chair.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (availability); Rehabilitation, vocational (suitability of program) (program chosen by worker)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a carpentry accident in July 1992, resulting in the amputation of the tips of two fingers and some loss of use of another finger.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits from September 1992 to January 1993.
The worker suffered a back injury in 1987 for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed denial of s. 147(2) supplementary benefits for periods from 1990 to 1992.
A 53-year-old jewellery maker suffered a back injury in June 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the worker's FEL award.

DecKeywords: Significant contribution (of compensable accident to disability)
DecSummary: A firefighter suffered a cervical and lumbar sprain when the fire engine in which he was riding struck a pole in 1983.  He suffered further compensable back injuries in falls in 1985 and 1988.  In 1986, the worker underwent surgery for decompression of the spinal cord at C5-6.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the cervical condition.

A company built and installed interiors in residences or businesses.  B suffered an injury while using a table saw resulting in amputation of two fingers.  The company appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement to B.  The issue was whether B was a worker or an independent operator.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in 1988 for which she was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147 supplementary benefits and VR services after the worker took early retirement in 1993.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a chest condition which she related to exposure to fumes in 1990 or an accident in 1991.

The worker was appealing denial of further benefits for organic disability.  The hearing was adjourned to wait for a final decision of the Board regarding entitlement for chronic pain, to allow the matter to be dealt with on a whole person basis.  [4 pages]

The worker appealed a decision denying entitlement.  In a preliminary matter, the Panel considered the admissibility of two medical reports submitted by the employer and the employer's request for additional medical evidence from the worker's doctor.
The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the employer breached its re-employment obligations when it terminated the worker's employment.

DecKeywords: Permanent impairment {NEL} (degree of impairment) (back); Permanent impairment {NEL} (rating schedule) (AMA Guides) (combined values)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting a 25% NEL award for back disability.
The worker suffered permanent impairment to her right arm, for which she was granted a 9% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming the 9% award.

The worker strained his neck when he overstretched while repairing a light bulb in March 1992.  He returned to work after one week.  In October 1992, the worker began receiving treatment for a shoulder condition which was later diagnosed as a rotator cuff tear.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the shoulder condition.

The worker received benefits until December 1, 1992, for conjunctivitis related to lead dust entering his eye on November 19, 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying continuous benefits until July 1993 for aggravation of a preexisting eye condition called pterygium.

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER account for three claims in which SIEF relief was granted after the three-year window for adjustments had closed.

DecKeywords: Investigation by Tribunal (post-hearing) (vocational rehabilitation assessment); Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a fracture of the tibia and fibula in 1986.  In 1990, he was awarded a 10% pension for leg disability.  He retrained as a welder but was unable to find a job.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147 supplementary benefits.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in December 1990.  She was granted a nominal FEL award in January 1992 and a rehabilitation supplement.  She returned to work but experienced further difficulties in December 1992.  She was granted a medical supplement while undergoing medical treatment until April 1, 1993.  She also received a vocational rehabilitation supplement from May 17, 1993, to July 23, 1993, while undergoing an FAE and an attempt to return to work on a graduated basis.  The worker's file was then closed and the supplement discontinued on the basis of the Board's finding that the worker was not restricted to working only four hours a day.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming denial of the supplement from April 1, 1993, to March 16, 1993, and from July 23, 1993, to June 6, 1994.

The worker suffered serious injuries, including compound fractures of his femur and wrist when he was pinned under a very heavy weight in 1981.  The worker appealed the earnings basis for calculation of benefits, the level of his pension and entitlement to a s. 147 supplement.  The Panel required additional medical evidence from a medical assessor.  [6 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in May 1990.  He returned to work a few months later but laid off a number of times due to back problems.  He returned to modified work with the accident employer in April 1992 as a spot welder but stopped working again in October 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying VR services and a s. 43(9) supplement after October 1992.

The worker was the manager of the physical plant at a facility for mentally disabled persons.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for stress-related disability which the worker claimed resulted from interpersonal difficulties with his new supervisor and lack of support and supervision for a special project which he was assigned to manage.

The employer appealed decisions of Appeals Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER account to reflect SIEF relief granted after expiry of the three-year cut-off date for retroactive adjustments.

The worker suffered from facet joint syndrome as a result of compensable accidents in 1985 and 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for an incident at home in 1990.

DecKeywords: Chronic obstructive lung disease; Silicosis; Smoking
DecSummary: The worker was an underground miner from 1956 to 1990, except for five years. The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension for silicosis.

The worker had a preexisting respiratory condition, a form of bronchitis, and preexisting asthma.  For a period of 13 months, starting in 1981 and ending when he stopped working in 1982, the worker worked indoors as a salesman in a small office with 12 co-workers, most of whom smoked and two of whom were chain smokers.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for aggravation of his preexisting condition from second-hand smoke.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (considering self totally disabled); Availability for employment (refusing suitable work); Permanent disability; Rehabilitation, medical (aid in getting worker back to work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered from simple silicosis in 1986 and 1987 as a result of exposure to silica dust in his work at a foundry.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% temporary partial disability benefits from August 1991 until his retirement at age 54 in August 1992, and denying a pension.
A caretaker in the public school system appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for back disability.

DecKeywords: Significant contribution (of compensable accident to disability)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a whiplash injury in a compensable motor vehicle accident in October 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary total benefits from May 1992 to May 1994.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (substantial new evidence) (medical literature)
DecSummary: The worker's widow applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying the worker benefits for lung cancer.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a hand injury in 1954 resulting in amputation of two fingers.  He was awarded a 9% pension.  This was increased to 10.5% in 1989 due to changes in the Rating Schedule.  In 1995, the Hearings Officer increased the pension to 14% due to development of additional symptoms.  This increase was retroactive to 1993.  The worker appealed.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (period of unemployment); Earnings basis (seasonal employment)
DecSummary: A construction worker suffered a compensable accident in October 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of benefits.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (suitability of program) (consultation); Suitable employment (consultation)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision closing her vocational rehabilitation file, following a failed return to work.

The worker was carrying heavy objects at work on February 1, 1992.  The Board initially granted entitlement for chest strain until February 14, 1992.  The Hearings Officer also granted entitlement for low back disability.  The employer appealed.
The worker suffered a back injury in July 1990.  He received temporary benefits until October 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits until July 1991.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Supplements, FEL (cooperation)
DecSummary: The worker was a heavy equipment operator in the construction industry.  He suffered a knee injury in a fall in 1991, for which he was awarded a 6% NEL award.  In July 1993, he was awarded a 26% FEL award.  In July 1994, VR services and supplementary benefits were discontinued.  In July 1995, at the R1 FEL review, he was granted only a sustainability award.  The worker appealed.

The worker suffered a shoulder strain in 1984 for which he was awarded a pension.  He also suffered a low back injury in 1985 for which he lost no time.  The worker appealed decisions of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement for shoulder and low back disability and denying entitlement for chronic pain.
The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER assessment.

The worker was digging and shovelling out a deep hole on November 21, 1991.  The Board granted benefits for low back disability until March 1992.  He was disabled after March 1992 by upper back disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the upper back disability.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (duration); Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (recalculation)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147(4) supplementary benefits after March 1992.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury while lifting in April 1992.  She returned to modified work in October 1992 and to full work in February 1993.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying SIEF relief.

The worker worked in a large downtown office building.  She completed her shift on December 11, 1992, and was leaving the building, walking down four steps outside the building when she slipped and fell.  The worker's employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a transfer of the costs of the accident to the company that was responsible for maintenance of the property.

The worker suffered a low back injury in a fall in March 1990.  He received a 5% FEL award in June 1991, increased to 37% in June 1993.  In May 1994, he was awarded an 18% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a FEL supplement under s. 43(9) after April 1994.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Significant contribution (of compensable accident to disability)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain arising after a fall at work in 1992.  On the evidence, the worker's life in Lebanon before he came to Canada was a significant contributing factor to his current psychological state.  However, he was able to find employment in Canada and to work without any difficulty prior to the accident.  The Panel concluded that the accident was also a significant contributing factor to the worker's condition.

The worker slipped and fell at work in February 1990.  He did not lose any time from work until 15 months later in May 1991.  In November 1991, he claimed entitlement for back disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker did not suffer a back injury in February 1990.

The worker appealed his 10% pension level.  He fell a distance of 18 feet in 1966, sustaining spinal fracturaces at T8 and T12.  He returned to different work one year later and continued to be gainfully employed for the next 20 years.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Withdrawal (of appeal)
DecSummary: The worker sought payment of the costs of a motorized scooter and the costs of a mobile phone to be used in case of emergency.  The worker was receiving a 52% pension covering multiple medical conditions.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (training) (unpaid placement); Worker (learner)
DecSummary: The employer operated day camps for children.  The employer also had a counsellor-in-training (CIT) program.  The appellant, a 15-year-old CIT, suffered a spinal injury causing partial quadriplegia when he slipped and fell.  The CIT appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer which denied entitlement for the accident on the basis that the CIT did not come within the definition of worker in the Act.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for cervical strain.  The worker was performing his regular work when he experienced a sharp pain.  There was no unusual movement or extra task being performed.  The worker had been doing this work for a year.  The work did involve stretching, bending and twisting but no heavy lifting.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered from overuse syndrome of the shoulder, elbow and wrist, for which she received temporary benefits for two years and a 9% pension.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying SIEF relief.

The worker's widow was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying dependency benefits.  This issue required a determination of whether the worker's death resulted from a compensable condition.  The hearing was adjourned to allow the worker's representative an opportunity to investigate the possibility of exposure to another substance.  [5 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in January 1991.  On October 14, 1992, a FEL adjudicator determined that the worker was capable of performing his normal work and that, accordingly, the worker was not entitled to a FEL award.  The date of the determination was November 1, 1992.  On appeal, the Hearings Officer found that the worker was only capable of working four hours per day.  The Hearings Officer granted a FEL award on that basis.  The worker appealed the amount of the FEL award.

The employer was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer granting initial entitlement for an accident.  The worker initially indicated that she would attend the hearing, but the worker's representative wrote to the Tribunal that the worker was stressed by the situation and did not want to attend.  The Panel convened a pre-hearing telephone conference to decide whether the worker should be summonsed to attend the hearing.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for loss of vision.  The Panel required additional medical evidence from a Tribunal medical assessor.  [3 pages]
A cashier appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome.  There was some doubt as to the correctness of the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome.

The worker appealed the level of his pension rating for a right ankle disability.  He fractured his ankle in 1983 when he tripped.  At the time of the first assessment in 1985, the worker's flexion and subtalar movements were found to be reduced by 50% and all movements were found to be painful.  This resulted in an award of 10%.  Given that according to the rating schedule total immobility warranted a 12% pension and that the worker had half the expected mobility, the worker's rating clearly took into account the degree of pain that he was experiencing.

A garbage collector appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for bilateral shoulder and right elbow disability.  On average, every day the worker lifted and threw 8,500 bags of garbage weighing about 30 pounds each.  The job was strenuous and repetitive.  The Panel concluded that the worker's condition was a disablement from the nature of his work.

DecKeywords: Fibromyalgia; Significant contribution (of employment to disability)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for neck and back pain, diagnosed as fibromyalgia, which she related to lifting pails at work in January 1992.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (substantial new evidence) (medical report)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeal Board denying ongoing entitlement for injuries resulting from an accident in 1971.
The worker's representative was absent for the hearing of the worker's appeal.  The worker stated that the representative told him the day before the hearing that he was unavailable.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [4 pages]
The hearing of the worker's appeal was adjourned due a death in the employer's family.  [3 pages]
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to a FEL supplement after a specific date.

The worker was requesting a commutation of his pension on the basis that the commutation was required to relieve him of the psychological burden associated with his debts.  Notes from the worker's psychiatrist stated that the worker had a psychological condition.
The appeal was adjourned to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for non-organic disability at the Board.  [3 pages]

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement for two periods in 1993.  Based on new evidence that was not available to the Hearings Officer, the Panel found that the worker continued to be disabled by his injuries during the periods in question.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming a 5% pension for elbow disability and granting only a 40% pension for chronic pain.

The worker was appealing the denial of ongoing temporary benefits subsequent to September 1992.  She had already been granted one withdrawal request in April 1994 to allow her to review her NEL assessment before proceeding.  The worker requested a second withdrawal after a recess in the May 1996 hearing during which her representative pointed out the problems with her evidence.  The worker's testimony had been frequently contradictory or at odds with the documentary evidence.  The Panel granted the worker's withdrawal request on the understanding that she could not return to the Tribunal at a later date with respect to these issues.  [5 pages]

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability from August 1991 to August 1992, denying a pension and denying supplementary benefits.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary total disability benefits for a period in 1990.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (pre-injury earnings) (planned reduction in wages)
DecSummary: The worker suffered an arm injury in an accident in March 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to a FEL award and denying entitlement for a psychiatric condition.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (medical examination) (employer request) (claim for compensation); Medical examination (employer request)
DecSummary: The worker applied for an order that she was not required to attend a medical examination by a doctor selected by the employer.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1963 and returned to work in 1964.  In 1966, he was assessed for a pension and found to have no residual impairment.  In 1979, he was awarded a 10% pension retroactive to 1978.  In 1980, the pension was increased to 15% and in 1991 was increased to 20%.
